status: Analysis choices recorded locally before new climate outcomes. Exploratory first regional panel, not externally preregistered confirmation or an animal result.
question: At approximately equal modeled daylength, do temperature and surface soil moisture change together or differently across regions?
frame: 72 fixed points: latitude -45,-30,-15,15,30,45 degrees and longitude -180 to 150 by 30 degrees. Static bundled Natural Earth land mask retained 21 land points before climate values. No relocation of desert, cropland, mountain, coastal or otherwise inconvenient points.
scope: Six latitude lines; no polar/equatorial coverage, not an area-weighted globally representative survey. Land-mask positional uncertainty retained.
hemisphere: North: March increasing and September decreasing in the same year. South: September increasing and next March decreasing, bracketing the December summer solstice.
matching: For each hemisphere/cycle, choose March date 17-25 and September date 17-29 with |modeled solar declination|<=1 degree, minimizing maximum modeled daylength mismatch over that hemisphere's preselected latitudes; ties by summed absolute declination then dates. Require max mismatch<=1 minute. Selection uses astronomy only. One paired day per site and cycle, not annual-average season effects.
source: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API; explicitly models=era5, timezone=auto; daily temperature_2m_mean, temperature_2m_max, soil_moisture_0_to_7cm_mean. Modeled weather/soil water, not field observation, vegetation, forage, animal activity or independent driver interventions.
contrasts: Decreasing minus increasing daylength branch, at each same requested point, using source local daily aggregates. Soil moisture in m3/m3 (dimensionless volume fraction); no interpretation as rainfall or plant-accessible biomass.
retention: Preserve all 21 sites and all 63 proposed pairs; failed or missing source stays explicitly unavailable. No new sites added after climate values, no signs selected and no source substitution.
summaries: Per-site three-cycle means and sign consistency; count opposite T/soil-water signs per available pair and per site mean. All changes descriptive; no p-values or population CIs; cycles within site and points within broad climate systems are dependent.
stop: One pilot only. Do not interpret 63 pairs as 63 independent regions or a global biological law. Satellite and scheduled animal-sensor extensions remain unexecuted future stages. Earlier Serengeti and GPS outputs are unchanged.
